item.text: {"text":"HSTU’s relative temporal attention bias encodes bucketed differences between observed event timestamps, alongside relative sequence position ([original paper](https://openreview.net/pdf?id=xye7iNsgXn)). Historical gaps Δij=|ti−tj| describe interaction spacing; the final history row captures age relative to the latest interaction, tn−ti. Neither supplies elapsed inactivity at recommendation time, tq−tn. Identical histories yield identical pairwise gaps whether queried immediately or months later. Thus historical gaps can support learned signals of changing interests within history, but cannot alone identify staleness caused by subsequent inactivity. This follows from the inputs, rather than being an empirical finding. Without an observable request timestamp, describe the mechanism as history-relative temporal modeling; never substitute the unavailable next-event timestamp.\n\nControlled ablations should retain one HSTU model per category, identical training budgets, seeds, splits and candidates: compare no bias, position-only, time-only and position-plus-time. Such component comparisons have precedent in [HSTU analysis](https://openreview.net/pdf?id=e6pqwHR1Yh). Replace timestamps with equally spaced events to test positional information; shuffle consecutive gaps within each history and reconstruct timestamps to preserve activity rate and gap distribution while disrupting their alignment with items. Normalize gaps by each history’s training-observed median and compare against a jointly trained rate-only feature to separate relative spacing from activity scale. Independently shift each history’s timestamp origin: pure pairwise-gap predictions should remain invariant, exposing absolute-calendar dependencies otherwise. Fit temporal preprocessing on training data only; audit prefix-only inputs and padding. If request time is genuinely available, vary tq while holding history fixed to isolate inactivity sensitivity; otherwise that effect is unidentifiable. Report category and macro validation HR@10; gains alone do not establish stale-interest detection."}
